root_cause: The datepicker does not hide when the input loses focus via keyboard navigation (Tab); it only hides on mouse click outside or similar events, leaving the calendar visible after tabbing away.
repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field that calls hide() on the datepicker when not inline, ensuring the calendar closes on focus loss via keyboard.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now close the datepicker by moving focus away with Tab, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Potential unintended hide if blur fires for reasons other than focus loss (e.g., popup opening), but guarded by !this.inline.
Inline pickers remain unaffected due to the inline check.
Duplicate hide calls may occur if other hide logic also runs on blur, but hide is idempotent.
verification_requirements: After typing a date and pressing Tab, the datepicker must close (.datepicker not visible).
Clicking on the datepicker or selecting a date via mouse/keyboard should still work and hide appropriately.
Inline datepickers should not be affected by the blur listener.
Focus should move to the next tabbable element (#instructions) as before.
